description: CRIT-004's passThreshold asserts a positive obligation ('Tier-3 live/testnet re-attack of the round-1 exploits MUST be executed by the adversary with its own new transaction hashes/timestamps') but its own enumerated FAIL list at the end of the same passThreshold only contains three triggers: (1) the gig test count is not exactly 48/48, (2) any of the three named FINDING tests is missing/renamed, or (3) 'the adversary substitutes the round-3 self-report for its own independent Tier-3 run.' None of these three triggers fires if the adversary simply never attempts ANY Tier-3 live re-attack at all (neither citing the round-3 report as a substitute, nor performing its own) -- it only fails the criterion if the adversary explicitly SUBSTITUTES the old report. A disk-only review that runs the 48 unit/integration tests, confirms the FINDING names, and never touches a live/testnet chain would trip zero of the three listed FAIL conditions, and could therefore be marked PASS under CRIT-004's own literal text -- directly contradicting REQ-103's BINDING acceptance criterion ('this re-attack MUST be independently executed by the Phase 3 adversary itself... a builder's own prior self-report is evidence of history, not a substitute for the fresh, independent re-verification this requirement demands', behavioral-spec.md:170-175) and verification-architecture.md's Gate item (3) ('the round-1 exploit scripts are re-attempted by the adversary itself, live, producing its own new transaction hashes', verification-architecture.md:144-148), both of which make Tier-3 live re-execution mandatory for REQ-103/PROP-103b, not merely 'nice to have.' The parenthetical at contract lines 76-77 ('explicitly out of scope for THIS sprint's binary pass: Tier-3 live re-execution is the Phase 3 adversary's own obligation to perform') is itself ambiguously worded -- read in isolation it can be misread as placing Tier-3 EXECUTION out of scope for the pass/fail decision, rather than placing reliance on the STALE round-3 report out of scope. This is precisely the kind of vague clause that allows grade inflation: a lenient or rushed Phase 3 adversary could legitimately claim compliance with CRIT-004's letter while skipping the one check (independent, live, on-chain re-attack of the self-verify and same-gig double-pay exploits) that this entire sprint's REQ-103/FIND-006 lineage exists to force.

evidence.snippet:
Tier-3 live/testnet re-attack of the round-1
      exploits MUST be executed by the adversary with its own new transaction hashes/timestamps -- a
      reference to `evidence/p2.2-security-fixes-round3.md` alone does NOT satisfy this criterion
      (explicitly out of scope for THIS sprint's binary pass: Tier-3 live re-execution is the Phase 3
      adversary's own obligation to perform, not something Phase 2 evidence can pre-satisfy). FAIL if
      the count is not exactly 48/48, if any of the three named FINDING tests is missing/renamed away,
      or if the adversary substitutes the round-3 self-report for its own independent Tier-3 run.

recommendation: Add an explicit fourth FAIL trigger to CRIT-004's passThreshold: 'FAIL if the adversary does not itself perform and document (its own tx hash(es)/timestamp(s), live or testnet) a fresh Tier-3 re-attack of the round-1 self-verify and same-gig double-pay exploits -- absence of any Tier-3 attempt is itself a FAIL, not merely a substitution of the round-3 report.' Also reword the parenthetical at lines 76-77 so it unambiguously scopes 'out of scope' to reliance on the round-3 report, not to Tier-3 execution itself.
